writes: all 256 bytes beginning at $fp, in ascending 32-bit word order

original.discovery_notes: Observed live when an active Endokuken record is released after contact. Other callers use the same routine to retire secondary objects. The name describes the proven record-level behavior without assuming a specific object type.

commands: flatpak run org.mamedev.MAME kinst -rompath assets/ki1 -debug -nodrc -debugscript mame/oracle_ki15d_880054d0.cmd -video none -sound none -nothrottle -skip_gameinfo -seconds_to_run 4 -cfg_directory work/mame/cfg -diff_directory work/mame/diff
verification.notes: Three controlled R4600 calls use different target addresses, fill bytes, and surrounding guard words. In every case MAME clears exactly 0x100 bytes and leaves $a2/$a3 one record past the target. The native test compares the complete 1 MiB mapped RAM image after each call.
